cards.back: Keeps its shape and does not flow. A stone is a solid.
cards.say: solid. Keeps its shape and does not flow. A stone is a solid.

cards.back: Flows and takes the shape of its container. Water is a liquid.
cards.say: liquid. Flows and takes the shape of its container. Water is a liquid.

cards.back: Spreads out to fill all the space it is in. Air is a gas.
cards.say: gas. Spreads out to fill all the space it is in. Air is a gas.

cards.back: A solid.
cards.say: Which state is a rock? A solid.

cards.back: A liquid.
cards.say: Which state is milk? A liquid.

cards.back: A gas.
cards.say: Which state is oxygen? A gas.

cards.back: A gas.
cards.say: Which state is steam? A gas.

cards.back: A solid.
cards.say: Which state is ice? A solid.

cards.back: A solid.
cards.say: Which state keeps its shape? A solid.

cards.front: Which state has a fixed volume but no fixed shape?
cards.back: A liquid.
cards.say: Which state has a fixed volume but no fixed shape? A liquid.

cards.front: Which state can be squashed into a smaller space?
cards.back: A gas.
cards.say: Which state can be squashed into a smaller space? A gas.

cards.front: Does a gas have a fixed shape?
cards.back: No. It spreads out to fill the container.
cards.say: Does a gas have a fixed shape? No. It spreads out to fill the container.

cards.back: A pencil, a brick and a book.
cards.say: Name three solids.. A pencil, a brick and a book.

cards.back: Water, milk and cooking oil.
cards.say: Name three liquids.. Water, milk and cooking oil.

cards.back: Air, oxygen and carbon dioxide.
cards.say: Name three gases.. Air, oxygen and carbon dioxide.

cards.front: Which state of matter does a drink in a cup belong to?
cards.back: A liquid, because it flows and takes the shape of the cup.
cards.say: Which state of matter does a drink in a cup belong to? A liquid, because it flows and takes the shape of the cup.

cards.front: Is a pencil a solid, a liquid or a gas?
cards.back: A solid, because it keeps its own shape.
cards.say: Is a pencil a solid, a liquid or a gas? A solid, because it keeps its own shape.

cards.front: Is sand a solid or a liquid?
cards.back: A solid. It can pour but each grain is solid.
cards.say: Is sand a solid or a liquid? A solid. It can pour but each grain is solid.

cards.front: Is a balloon full of air a solid, liquid or gas?
cards.back: The air inside is a gas.
cards.say: Is a balloon full of air a solid, liquid or gas? The air inside is a gas.

cards.front: Why can we not see most gases?
cards.back: Gases like air are clear, so they cannot be seen.
cards.say: Why can we not see most gases? Gases like air are clear, so they cannot be seen.

cards.front: How can you show that air takes up space?
cards.back: Blow up a balloon. The air fills it.
cards.say: How can you show that air takes up space? Blow up a balloon. The air fills it.

cards.front: A liquid is poured into a tall glass then a wide bowl. What stays the same?
cards.back: The amount (volume), not the shape.
cards.say: A liquid is poured into a tall glass then a wide bowl. What stays the same? The amount (volume), not the shape.
